slides.title: Five law firm brands worth [learning from.]
slides.lede: Ten examples in the full guide. Here are five, each showing a different branding decision, from a repeatable promise to one simple visual device.

slides.title: One promise, ["For the People"], on every channel
slides.note: **Establish the promise before designing the campaign.** A slogan cannot compensate for an unclear proposition.

slides.title: Refresh a heritage identity without losing its [recognition]

cards.label: Keep
cards.text: The heritage and the recognition the name already carries.

cards.label: Refresh
cards.text: A refined monogram, Domaine typography and a refreshed digital presence.

slides.quote: Write for the people who need legal services, not simply for the lawyers who provide them.
slides.text: Bend Law Group speaks to small-business owners with approachable messaging, including "Dream Big. We got your back.", rather than legal terminology and lists of credentials.

slides.title: One simple [red line], applied consistently everywhere
slides.text: A simple brandmark and a recurring red-line graphic run across the website, corporate identity and social media. A simple graphic device, used with discipline, can do the job.

slides.title: Research shaped the positioning. Positioning shaped the [design].

items.title: Stakeholder interviews and research
items.text: The brand refresh began with qualitative research.

items.title: Verbal and visual identity
items.text: Positioning informed how the firm looks and sounds.

items.title: Carried into communications
items.text: Website, video, brochures, stationery and templates.

slides.title: The commercial idea should lead the creative work.
